answer.rationale: Primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line has no buffer, so deferral or leaving primary coverage open would raise delivery risk. A primary switch is not justified on current evidence: c2’s ‘quick onboarding’ is a different context and is unverified against a 14-day, 94%-loaded cutover. Adding a second source (c3) addressed a shortage/SPOF, not an expiring primary or an 18% spend cut, and would consume the only decision without securing continuity. Incumbent mid-cycle refusal makes a price reopen uncertain, but formal expiry is the renewal window where c4 and a multi-year volume structure (c6) previously moved unit cost without shrinking scope or forcing migration (c1). Intend a term/volume negotiation aimed at TCO, not a vendor change; treat c4/c6 as hypotheses until the archive is checked. Flag line-stoppage risk if signature slips past day 14.
